title: LANGTRAJ: Diffusion Model and Dataset for Language-Conditioned Trajectory Simulation

control_signal.value: Natural-language descriptions of agent behaviour (e.g. yield to the right, merge left), with agents rephrased as target agent and other agents; optional adversarial collision guidance.

control_mechanism.value: Text cross-attention in the denoiser to per-agent language embeddings (DistilBERT with LoRA, trained end-to-end); text dropout in training enables classifier-free guidance; gradient guidance can be added post-training.

base_model.value: Scene-diffusion model with query-centric GNN scene encoder and stacked transformer denoiser (inter-agent attention, agent-context cross-attention, text cross-attention); closed-loop training, distilled from K=100 to K=5 steps.

datasets.value: INTERDRIVE (new: human interaction labels on Waymo and nuPlan plus heuristic single-agent labels) and ProSim-Instruct-520k; validated on Waymo Open Motion Dataset.

metrics.value: WOSAC Meta, kinematic, interactive, map realism; controllability as minADE improvement over unconditioned model; collision rate and kinematic/map scores for safety-critical runs.

controllability_evidence.value: Direct text conditioning gives mADE 2.29 versus 2.65 unconditioned and 2.70 for CTG++-style LLM guidance. Safety-critical: collision rate 0.43 versus 0.33 for LLM-based guidance.

stated_limitations.value: Failures often arise when language conflicts with recent history; the model prioritises history, especially for static vehicles. minADE may not capture instruction adherence. Strong CFG weights degrade map adherence.

notes: Text is trained in directly, in contrast to LLM-written guidance; collision guidance is an additional inference-time option. Safety-critical collision rate of 0.43 is a fraction in the table; the text says rates as high as 40%.
